sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Neo-Vedanta**: A modern interpretation of Advaita Vedanta that emphasizes social service and practical application over ascetic withdrawal.
• **Practical Vedanta**: The belief that divinity exists in every human; therefore, serving humanity is equivalent to worshipping God (Daridra Narayana).
• **Universalism**: Advocated for the harmony of all religions, asserting that all paths lead to the same ultimate truth.
• **Nationalism**: Defined nationalism as a spiritual force rooted in India's cultural heritage, emphasizing self-reliance and strength.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Social Reform**: Opposed caste-based discrimination and advocated for women's education and empowerment.
• **Cultural Nationalism**: Used the 'Glory of the Past' to instill pride and confidence in the Indian youth against colonial inferiority.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Balancing traditional orthodoxy with modern rationalism.
• **Solutions**: Adopting his 'Practical Vedanta' to address contemporary issues like poverty, inequality, and communalism.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-R-E-E-D'
• **Decoded Meaning**: C-Chicago (1893), R-Ramakrishna Mission (1897), E-Education (Man-making), E-Equality (Caste/Gender), D-Daridra Narayana.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Vivekananda did NOT support the abolition of the caste system by law; he advocated for the removal of caste-based 'privileges' and 'inequality' through spiritual and social awakening.
Mains Value Addition: Use the quote 'Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached' in essays regarding youth empowerment or national development.

keyTakeaways: Vivekananda was a bridge between ancient Indian wisdom and modern Western rationalism.
His philosophy of 'Practical Vedanta' shifted the focus of religion from ritualism to social service.
He was a key architect of modern Indian identity, emphasizing strength, fearlessness, and self-reliance.
